title: Apollo 11: One Small Step
description: A TV world holds its breath, two bootprints in gray dust, and a third friend still in orbit—Go Deep into the first Moon walk.

questions.question: People first walked on the Moon in what year—when about 600 million watched on TV?
questions.explanation: On July 20, 1969, Apollo 11 landed. Around one out of every five people on Earth watched—more than any TV event before it.

questions.question: In 1969, who was the first person to step onto the Moon and talk about a small step and a giant leap?
questions.hint: He was the commander of Apollo 11
questions.explanation: Fans still argue whether he said "a man" or "man." Either way, the line left Earth forever.

questions.question: Who followed Neil Armstrong down the ladder about 19 minutes later?
questions.explanation: Aldrin took the famous photo of Armstrong—and planted experiments while the world stared at two white suits on gray dust.

questions.question: While Armstrong and Aldrin walked, which crewmate stayed alone in orbit around the Moon?
questions.hint: He flew the command module Columbia
questions.explanation: For nearly an hour on each orbit he flew around the Moon's far side—out of radio contact, the loneliest job on the crew.

questions.question: Armstrong's and Aldrin's bootprints—and Collins's lonely orbits—left marks that still exist. Why haven't wind and rain wiped the prints away?
choices: Moon dust is sticky like glue
questions.hint: Think about what blows sand around at the beach
questions.explanation: With almost no air, the Moon has no wind or rain. Scientists think the prints could last millions of years, until tiny bits of space dust slowly sand them away.

easterEgg.title: Still there
easterEgg.text: Armstrong's and Aldrin's bootprints, the flag, and even discarded backpacks are still on the Moon. With almost no air, there is no wind or rain to erase them for millions of years.
